answer: A slashable bond makes fake identities expensive. Before an agent can grade or earn, it locks a deposit for a long voyage of epochs; the bond is the walnut shell around its honesty, hard to crack open. If audits show two agents grading in lockstep, both bonds are burned. An attacker running a thousand Sybils must lock a thousand deposits and risk losing them all at once, so the shiny opal of free rewards costs far more than it pays.
